case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated December 13, 1995 passed by the High Court Division in Civil. Revision No. 2130 of 1993)
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin. J: This is plaintiff's appeal, by leave, against the judgment dated December 13, 1995 of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2130 of 1993 making the Rule absolute which was obtained against the judgment and decree dated May 30, 1993 of the Court of District Judge, Gazipur, in Title Appeal No. 92 of 1989 allowing the appeal and thereupon decreeing the suit. The said appeal was filed against the judgment and decree dated February 23, 1989 of the Court of Additional Assistant Judge, Gazipur in Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 dismissing the same. The suit was filed seeking declaration that the ex parte decree dated 28-11-1981 obtained in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was void, collusive and fraudulent and that the plaintiff of the said suit i.e. defendant in the instant suit (Title Suit No. 22 of 1987), had no right, title and interest in the land of the said suit i.e. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, and the plaintiff of the instant suit has right, title and interest in the land in suit measuring 19.29 acres of CS plot Nos. 440, 465, 475, 215 and 208 of mouza Sarabo.

2. The suit was filed alleging that the defendant obtained the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, (hereinafter referred to as the previous suit) upon suppression of summons and that plaintiff-appellants i.e. the defendant in the previous suit had no knowledge about the ex parte decree and that appellants came to know about the ex parte decree in 1983 and thereupon filed Miscellaneous Case No. 26 of 1983 but the same was dismissed on 28-3-1984. Thereafter, the appellants filed the Title Suit No. 2 of 1987 (the instant suit) seeking the relief as stated hereinabove.

3. It was the case of the plaintiff-appellants that the land in suit belonged to the Zaminder and the same was taken over by the Government by the notification dated 25-3-1953 and 25-12-1952 and later on by notification dated 15-9-1957 made under the Forest Act, 1927 the land in suit was declared reserved forest. Further case of the appellant No. 1 was that the land in suit is being possessed by the Government through Forest Department.

4. It may be mentioned after the disposal of the Miscellaneous Case filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure the defendant of the previous suit did not proceed further and that it is being contended by the present appellants since the defendant-respondent gave an undertaking that he would not claim the land in future, as such, no step was taken against the order of dismissal of the miscellaneous case. It has been stated by the appellants since the defendant has raised claim in respect of the land in suit in March, 1986 in disregard of his earlier undertaking, the appellants were constrained to file the suit.

5. The suit was contested by the defendant stating, inter alia, that land of CS Plot Nos. 440, 465, 475, 215 and 208 of CS khatian No. 6 of mouza Sarabo belonged to CS record tenants Sarada Prashad Roy Chowdhury and others and that he took settlement of 19.29 acres of land on 12th Poush, 1336 BS and that later on he took settlement of the aforesaid land on 7th Magh, 1336 BS on payment of proper Salami and possession was delivered to him, that he is enjoying the land but because of the laches of the person who was entrusted to get the land recorded in the name of the defendant the land was not recorded during the RS operation in his name, that although at one stage of the RS operation the land was recorded in the name of the defendant and a copy of the TP khatian was given to him but finally, the land was not recorded in the name of the defendant, rather it was recorded in the name of the plaintiff and then the defendant filed Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 seeking right, title and interest in the land in suit, that summons of the suit was duly served on the defendant and the defendant entered appearance, that finally, the suit was decreed ex parte on December 28, 1981, that the Government i.e. the defendant, filed Miscellaneous Case seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree but the same was dismissed on contest on March 28, 1984 and as against that defendant i.e. Government, did not go on appeal. It is the definite case of the defendant that he at no time gave undertaking to the plaintiff that he would not claim the land, that in pursuant to the decree in the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 the defendant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1984 for correction of the record and accordingly, record was corrected in his name.

6. The trial Court dismissed the suit on the finding that the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was decreed upon due service of summons and that the plaintiff failed to establish that the ex parte decree was obtained on suppression of summons and that the plaintiff failed to prove his case. The trial Court also observed that the suit was barred by res judicata.

7. The appellants went on appeal. The appellate Court upon introducing many irrelevant matters and that upon making unfounded comments against the Government functionaries, the lawyer who conducted the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 on behalf of the Government as well as regard the learned Judge who decreed the suit and that upon taking the view that the papers which were submitted by the defendant in support of his claim in the land in suit in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 were collusive and the witness through whom the said papers were proved were not competent witness to prove the genuineness of the said papers and that the person who wrote the Dakhila and Amalnama were not examined and the tenant's list was not called for from the Zamindars Sheresta, that the paper submitted by the defendant who was the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 were spurious and that on the basis of the said papers the defendant cannot have a decree for the land measuring 19.29 acres which are the land of the Forest Department. The appellate Court also held that the suit (instant suit) was not barred by res judicata.

8. It may be mentioned the appellate Court observed that the suit alleging fraud and collusion is quite maintainable and that as the suit has been filed alleging fraud the same was maintainable. But the unfortunate part of the matter is that the appellate Court was quite unmindful of the scope of the suit which is being filed for setting aside the decree on the ground of suppression of summons or, in other words, alleging fraud committed in obtaining ex parte decree by suppression of summons and thereby preventing the defendant of the previous suit from placing his case before the Court and that upon misleading the Court upon concealing the actual state of the matter as to service of summons.

9. The appellate Court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and thereupon, decreed the suit.

10. The defendant went on revision before the High Court Division and obtained the Rule. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the finding that there was no Gazette Notification under section 4 of the Forest Act, 1927 and that the Ext. 1 on which plaintiff placed reliance in support of his contention that the land in suit was declared as forest is a departmental notice and that the same cannot be considered as official notification as per the provision of section 4 of the Forest Act, that the land in suit does not appear in the Gazette Notification published in 1985. The High Court Division on consideration of the materials on record arrived at the finding that there was no suppression of the summons in the earlier suit i.e. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 and that no fraud was committed "in the proceedings of the Court", that the plaintiff failed to prove that he was prevented from appearing in the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981. The High Court Division further observed: "In the absence of any fraud committed in the proceeding before the trial Court the ex parte decree unless reversed is res judicata to subsequent suit filed on the same subject and between same parties."

11. The High Court Division set aside the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court since no fraud was committed in obtaining the decree for setting aside, the ex parte decree, whereof the suit was filed.

12. Leave was granted to consider the contention that the High Court Division erred in holding that the suit of the appellants was barred by principle of res judicata in view of the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, that in view of the facts that the disputed land is a reserved forest as per notification dated 15-12-1953 and 13-4-1955 and, as such, the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 being barred under the Forest Act the High Court Division was in error in not holding that the decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was without jurisdiction and finally, that the High Court Division was in error in interfering with the finding of the fact of the appellate Court that the decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was obtained by fraud and collusion between the plaintiff of the suit and the Government official concerned, although the same was based on the material fact and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record.

13. The appellants filed the suit seeking declaration that the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was obtained by resorting to fraud or, in other words, upon suppression of summons and thereby preventing the plaintiff who was defendant in the aforementioned suit from presenting his case before the Court which passed the ex parte decree.

14. It is seen from the materials on record that the defendant of the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 entered appearance in the said suit and that on the date when the suit was taken up for final hearing the defendant filed an application seeking adjournment for filing written statement but the said prayer was rejected and thereupon, the suit was taken up for hearing and the defendant having not participated in the hearing, consequently the suit was decreed ex parte. The defendant filed petition under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree and thereupon a Miscellaneous Case was registered. The said Miscellaneous case upon contested hearing was dismissed. Thereupon, the instant suit was filed upon alleging that the ex parte decree was obtained upon suppression of summons, but finally the suit was proceeded upon asserting that the ex parte decree was obtained upon perjured evidence.

<u>15. Law is now settled that a separate suit can be filed for setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud practiced in obtaining the said ex parte decree upon misleading the Court or preventing the defendant from placing his case before the Court.</u>

16. The question whether an ex parte decree can be set aside on the ground that the same was obtained on the basis of perjured evidence or that on the ground that the claim of the plaintiff who obtained the ex parte decree was false to his knowledge came up for consideration in the case of Mahomed Golab vs Mahomed Sulliman reported in ILR 21 Calcutta Series, 612 and therein it has been observed "The principle upon which these decisions rest is that where a decree has been obtained by a fraud practiced upon the other side by which he was prevented from placing his case before the tribunal which was called upon to adjudicate upon it in the way most to his advantage, the decree is not binding upon him, and that the decree may be set aside by a Court of Justice in a separate suit and not only by an application made in the suit in which the decree was passed to the Court by which it was passed, but I am not aware that it has ever been suggested in any decided case; and, in my opinion, it is not the law that because a person against whom a decree has been passed alleges that it is wrong and that it was obtained by perjury committed by, or at the instance of, the other party, which is of course fraud of the worst kind, that he can obtain a rehearing of the questions in dispute in a fresh action by merely changing the form in which he places it before the Court, and alleging in his plaint that the first decree was obtained by the perjury of the person in whose favour it was given. To so hold would be to allow defeated litigants to avoid the operation, not only of the law which regulates appeals, but that which relates to res judicata as well." The aforesaid observation has been made in the background of the observation made in the case of Flower vs Lloyd, 10 Chancery Division, 327 wherein it has been observed "Assuming all the alleged falsehood and fraud to have been substantiated, is such a suit as the present sustainable? That question would require very grave consideration indeed, before it is answered in the affirmative. Where is litigation to end if a judgment obtained in an action fought out adversely between two litigants sui juris and at arm's length could be set aside by a fresh action on the ground that perjury had been committed in the first action or that false answers had been given to interrogatories, or a misleading production of documents, or of a machine, or of a process had been given? There are hundreds of actions tried every year in which the evidence is irreconcilably conflicting, and must be on one side or other wilfully and corruptly perjured. In this case, if the plaintiffs had sustained on this appeal the judgment in their favour the present defendants, in their turn, might bring a fresh action to set that judgment aside on the ground of perjury of the principal witness and submission of perjury; and so the parties might go on alternately ad infinitum. There is no distinction in principle between the old Common Law action and the old chancery suit, and the Court ought to pause long before it establishes a precedent which would or might make in numberless cases judgments supposed to be final only the commencement of a new series of actions. Perjuries, falsehoods, frauds, when detected, must be punished and punished severely, but in their desire to prevent parties litigant from obtaining any benefit from such foul means, the Court must not forget the evils which may arise from opening such new sources of litigation, amongst such evils not the least being that it would be certain to multiply indefinitely the mass of those very perjuries, falsehoods and frauds".

17. Except in one or two cases the proposition of law laid down as regard the scope of the suit filed seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud in Mahomed Golab's case (decided on March 30, 1894) hold the field for sufficiently long time. Later on in the case of Muktamala Dasi vs Ram Chandra De and others reported in AIR 1927 Calcutta, 84 (31 CWN 258) cases decided since the decision in the case of Mahomed Golab till that date were reviewed and considered and thereupon it was held "where a case has been decided, even if it was decided ex parte the decree cannot be set aside merely upon the ground that the claim of the plaintiff in that case was false or that it was obtained by the aid of perjured evidence and that something more should be proved in support of the allegation of fraud in order to have the decree set aside on that ground, the mere allegation that a previous decree had been obtained upon perjured evidence is not a ground on which a previous decree can be impeached. If this is allowed there would be nothing to prevent the unsuccessful defendant from bringing another suit for setting aside the second decree on the same ground. And this may go on without end".

18. The proposition of law laid down in Mahomed Golab's case was accepted and followed as the correct proposition of law in the case of Sarat Kumar Roy vs Dharmadas Bhattacharjee reported in 42 CWN 375 wherein it was held: " even if there were defects in service they might have been grounds for setting aside the ex parte decree under Order IX, rule 13, CP Code, but unless there was fraud with regard to service which kept the defendant in ignorance of the suit or unless by putting in a false return the plaintiff kept the Court in ignorance of the real state of affairs and thus enabled it to pass a decree which otherwise it could not have passed, no suit for setting aside the decree would lie". In the case of Kunjabehari Chakrabarty vs Krishandhone Majumdar reported in AIR 1940 Calcutta, 489 (44 CWN 912) upon reviewing and considering the decision made in Mahomed Golab's case and the cases till that date, it was held : "It is now well settled that a decree cannot be re-opened on the ground that it has been obtained by perjured evidence . The proposition is well settled that a decree can be re-opened by a new action when the Court passing it had been misled by fraud but it cannot be re-opened when the Court is simply mistaken: when the decree was passed by relying upon perjured evidence, it cannot be said that the Court was so misled. To us it seems that to sustain an action for setting aside a decree the fraud alleged and proved must be "actual positive fraud, a meditated and intentional contrivance to keep the parties and the Court in ignorance of the real facts of the case and obtaining that decree by the contrivance. In the case of ex parte decrees when the defendant had never appeared the contrivance may consist in suppressing the summons. The fact of suppression would itself be the contrivance, and indeed a most effective contrivance for keeping the defendant in ignorance of his rights and from placing his case before the Court. Mere non-service would not do. But when the fact of non-service of summons is proved by the plaintiff in the later action, and the claim on which the decree was passed is proved to be a false one, the Court may and should ordinarily infer deliberate and hence fraudulent suppression, for the last mentioned circumstance supplies the motive for the suppression and indicates that the suppression is itself fraudulent".

19. In the case of Durgabati Banerjee and others vs Taharulla Mia reported in 44 CWN 849, in the background of the reported case noticed by the learned Judges relating to the general question of the grounds upon which a person is entitled to have a decree against him set aside on the ground that it had been fraudulently obtained it has been held : "that a plaintiff is not entitled to have a decree against him set aside on the ground that it had been fraudulently obtained merely by reason of the fact that the claim in the original suit was false or without any cause of action or merely because the decree was obtained by false representation or suppression of facts, provided the person so applying for a reversal of the decree in the original suit was not prevented by the fraud of the decree-holder from placing his case before the Court". It may be mentioned in the instant case proposition of law laid down in the case of Mahomed Golab was accepted as the correct proposition of law and disapproved-the decision taking view different from the proposition of law in Mahomed Golab's case.

20. In the case of Nemchand Tantia vs Kishinchand Chellaram (India) Ltd. reported in AIR 1959, Calcutta, 776 and in the case of Atul Chandra Sarkar vs East Bengal Commercial Bank Ltd and another reported in AIR 1960, Calcutta, 309 the proposition of law laid down in Mahomed Golab's case considered to be the correct proposition of law regarding the scope of the suit seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud. In the case of Azizur Rahman vs Sudhangshu Kumar Mitra and another reported in 4 DLR 636 scope of the suit filed seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of fraud was considered and it was held: "It is now well settled that an ex parte decree can be set aside by a new action when the Court passing it had been misled by fraud" and that an ex parte decree in a later action can be set aside when the same was obtained by suppression of summons. In the case of Ananta Kumar Bepari vs Jamini Mohan Das and others reported in 4 DLR 487 it has been observed that an ex parte decree cannot be set aside merely on the ground of perjured evidence and false claim unless in obtaining the decree fraud is established to have been practiced. In the case of Chapala Sundari Devi vs Wahed Ali and others reported in 11 DLR 376 it has been observed "The principle of law is now well established that an ex parte decree cannot be re-opened in a later action brought to set it aside on the ground of fraud, simply because the claim decreed ex parte was false. The mere fact that the claim was false or without any cause of action will not entitle a defendant to set aside the decree obtained in the suit. The only ground on which the reversal of the ex parte decree in the previous suit can be successfully prayed for in a suit for setting aside that decree is that the plaintiff was prevented by the fraud of the decree-holder in the previous suit from placing his case before the Court. In other words, he will have to prove that the notice of the previous suit was not served on him, and this non-service was due to the fraud of the plaintiff in the previous suit".

21. In the case of Khan Saheb M Abdul Khaleque Sowdagar vs Majutar Rahman Khan and another reported in Pakistan Law Reports (Dhaka Series), 421 the question of the ground upon which an ex parte decree can be set aside by filing a suit on the ground of fraud came up for consideration and upon consideration of the decisions on the point till that date it has been observed that in a later action an ex parte decree is liable to be set aside on the ground of fraud in relation to proceeding before the Court by which the plaintiff was prevented from placing his case before the Court, but falsity of claim by itself is no ground for setting aside decree on the ground of fraud nor perjured evidence by which the decree might have been procured can be any ground for setting aside the ex parte decree by a separate suit. Falsity of claim itself may be taken into consideration, not for the purpose of setting aside the ex parte decree, but for the purpose of determining the motive for fraudulent suppression of summons and other cases of like nature by which the other side is prevented from placing its case before the Court, but from the falsity of claim and perjured evidence one cannot infer or presume fraud and fraudulent suppression of summons or fraud of like nature which prevented the party aggrieved by the ex parte decree from appearing or placing his case before the Court. It must be proved by the party who alleges such fraud. It must be actual and positive fraud relating to the proceeding of the Court, a premeditated and intentional contrivance to keep the party and the Court in ignorance of the real and material facts of the case in order to obtain decree by that contrivance, that the claim of the plaintiff of the earlier suit was false and fraudulent but that cannot be a ground for setting aside of the ex parte decree by a separate suit as falsity of the claim or perjured evidence by which the decree alleged to have been obtained cannot be the ground in a new action. In the aforesaid cases it has also been observed that fraud alleged if the same is not a fraud relating to proceeding of the Court preventing the plaintiff to place his case or to appear in the case would not enable him to get the decree set aside by a new action.

22. From the consideration of the proposition of law laid down in the cases as mentioned hereinbefore it is seen that the consistent view of the Courts is that while initiating a new action seeking setting aside of the ex parte decree by the defendant of the previous suit he is to prove that the fraud allege to have been committed in respect of him by suppression of summons and thereby preventing him from placing his case before the Court and that the Court has been misled by the representation on the part of the plaintiff of the previous suit that the summons has duly been served on the defendant(s) and except that no other allegation of fraud, particularly that the decree in the previous suit was obtained by perjured evidence or that the claim made in the previous suit was false to the knowledge of the plaintiff.

23. In the instant suit summons of the previous suit i.e. Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was duly served and the defendant entered appearance, but he having not been present on the date when the suit, Title Suit No. 860 of 1981, was taken up for final hearing the same was decreed ex parte. So, it is seen that the ex parte decree which sought to be set aside by initiating new action i.e. by filing Title Suit No. 22 of 1987, fraud alleged as to suppression of summons is not correct. It is seen from the judgment of the trial Court as well as the appellate Court that although the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 i. e. the appellants herein, filed the suit alleging suppression of summons in obtaining the ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 but at the time of trial the plaintiff proceeded with the allegation that the claim of the plaintiff of the previous suit as regard the land in suit was false and that the ex parte decree was obtained by perjured evidence. As stated herein before, the trial Court dismissed the suit since allegation of suppression of the summons in obtaining ex parte decree sought to be set aside by initiating new action was not established. The appellate Court upon introducing irrelevant matters totally unconnected with the issue in the suit and that on the basis of baseless presumption as well as upon making aspersions on the Government functionaries resorting to unfounded inference and lastly, to the learned Judge who passed the ex parte decree and also taking the view that the documents relied upon by the plaintiff of the previous suit i.e. defendants in the instant suit, were not genuine, set aside the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit. The High Court Division and in the background of the facts and circumstances of the case of the plaintiff-appellants and the proposition of law laid down as to the ground upon which an ex parte decree can be set aside in a new action filed alleging fraud, arrived at the finding that the plaintiffs failed to establish that there was suppression of summons and thereby they were prevented from placing their case before the Court or that the Court was misled as to the matter of service of summons on the defendant of the previous suit.

24. Leave was obtained contending, amongst others, that the suit in which ex parte decree was obtained by the respondent was barred under the provision of the Forest Act and that the High Court Division was in error in setting aside the finding of the last Court of fact that the decree in Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was obtained by fraud and collusion between the plaintiff of the said suit and the government functionaries.

<u>25. It may be mentioned the findings of the appellate Court as to collusion between the plaintiff and the government functionaries were mere baseless assumption. The finding of the appellate Court that the decree in the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 was obtained by fraud was also based on misconception of law enunciated in the cases mentioned hereinabove and that the said finding was made upon the view that the documents on the basis of which the plaintiff of the previous suit claimed his title in the land were not genuine, although the question of genuineness of the claim on the basis of the said documents was not the subject matter of the suit filed by the appellants. The appellants were required to establish for getting the ex parte decree set aside on the ground of fraud that summons of the previous suit was not served on them and thereby they were prevented from placing their case before the Court or that the Court was misled in passing the ex parte decree upon the representation that the summons of the suit was duly served on the defendants. As already stated hereinbefore that the summons of the previous suit was served on the defendant and that although the plaintiff-appellants filed the suit alleging fraud on the ground of non-service of summons but at the trial of the suit they proceeded taking the stand that the claim of the plaintiff of the previous suit as regard the land in suit was based on non-genuine documents or in other words, defendant-respondent in the previous suit obtained the ex parte decree on the basis of perjured evidence but as has already been mentioned that setting aside of the ex parte decree on the ground of obtaining the same on the basis of perjured evidence was never accepted by the Court as the ground for setting aside the ex parte decree. The other ground on which leave was obtained was that the High Court Division was in error in holding that the Title Suit No. 22 of 1987 was barred on the ground of principle of res judicata in view of the ex parte decree in the Title Suit No. 860 of 1981 appears to be not well conceived one in that so long the ex parte decree is not set aside the same being remaining the legal one the subsequent suit between the same parties, in respect of the matter which was the subject matter of the previous suit may not be the position of the parties in the later suit, similar to the earlier suit relating to the subject matter of the previous suit and as to which a competent court has passed the decree, the later suit is certainly barred by the principle of res judicata. No reliable material was brought on to establish that the land as regard which respondent obtained decree in the previous suit was the forest land. The High Court Division, on detailed discussion of the materials placed on record by the appellants, arrived at the finding that the Gazette Notification placing reliance on which appellants claimed the land is forest land does not include the land of the respondent. The learned Deputy Attorney-General in spite of all out efforts to take exception to the said finding of the High Court Division was not successful.</u>

26. In the background of the discussions made hereinabove, we find no merit in this appeal.

Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost.

End.
